knowledge_points.statement: This study asks whether copper doping improves CO2 photoreduction over titania under visible light.
We prepared Cu-doped TiO2 samples by sol-gel and tested them in a batch photoreactor at 25 °C.
Solar-driven CO2 reduction offers a route to carbon-neutral fuels, but pristine TiO2 absorbs mainly ultraviolet light.
Whether transition-metal doping shifts the absorption edge while preserving selectivity remains an open question for dilute copper loadings.
We synthesized Cu-doped TiO2 with nominal Cu loadings of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 wt% using sol-gel, and analyzed phase composition by XRD.
Samples were tested in a 100 mL batch photoreactor under 420 nm cut-off illumination at 25 °C and 1 bar, with CO and CH4 quantified by gas chromatography.
The 1.0 wt% sample reached a CO selectivity of 92% and a CO yield of 14 umol g-1 h-1, whereas the undoped reference reached only 61% selectivity.
XRD showed no detectable CuO phase at 0.5 and 1.0 wt%, indicating that copper remains highly dispersed in the titania lattice.
At 2.0 wt% loading, selectivity decreased to 74% and CH4 became detectable, suggesting that agglomerated copper sites favor deeper reduction.
These results indicate that dilute copper doping extends visible-light absorption without sacrificing CO selectivity.
This study is limited to one batch reactor and 4 h runs; stability beyond 24 h and the effect of humidity were not examined.
Future work should test the catalysts under solar-spectrum illumination and quantify copper speciation by XAS.

sources.quote: This study asks whether copper doping improves CO2 photoreduction over titania under visible light.
We prepared Cu-doped TiO2 samples by sol-gel and tested them in a batch photoreactor at 25 °C.
The doped catalyst reached a CO selectivity of 92% at 25 °C, while the undoped reference reached 61%.
Solar-driven CO2 reduction offers a route to carbon-neutral fuels, but pristine TiO2 absorbs mainly ultraviolet light.
Whether transition-metal doping shifts the absorption edge while preserving selectivity remains an open question for dilute copper loadings.
We synthesized Cu-doped TiO2 with nominal Cu loadings of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 wt% using sol-gel, and analyzed phase composition by XRD.
Samples were tested in a 100 mL batch photoreactor under 420 nm cut-off illumination at 25 °C and 1 bar, with CO and CH4 quantified by gas chromatography.
The 1.0 wt% sample reached a CO selectivity of 92% and a CO yield of 14 umol g-1 h-1, whereas the undoped reference reached only 61% selectivity.
XRD showed no detectable CuO phase at 0.5 and 1.0 wt%, indicating that copper remains highly dispersed in the titania lattice.
At 2.0 wt% loading, selectivity decreased to 74% and CH4 became detectable, suggesting that agglomerated copper sites favor deeper reduction.
These results indicate that dilute copper doping extends visible-light absorption without sacrificing CO selectivity.
The improvement is consistent with copper acting as a shallow trap that suppresses charge recombination, although the evidence here is indirect.
This study is limited to one batch reactor and 4 h runs; stability beyond 24 h and the effect of humidity were not examined.
Future work should test the catalysts under solar-spectrum illumination and quantify copper speciation by XAS.
